rules.statement: Declare static data (static fields and static properties) before instance members, after constants, in test code as well as production code, but don't report static methods declared after instance members.
rules.why: The member-order convention's "statics at the top" means static data; static methods may sit with the instance code they serve.
rules.check: Look for a static field or static property declared below an instance field or member. Don't raise a finding for a static method placed after instance members.

rules.statement: When an implementation refuses inputs beyond a fixed limit (for example a maximum number of key segments), state that limit in the XML documentation of the interface member it implements.
rules.why: Callers and other implementers can't tell from the contract that over-long inputs are refused.
rules.check: Compare limits enforced in the implementation with the interface's <param> or <summary> text, and with sibling interfaces that already document the same limit.

rules.statement: Don't ask for <exception cref> entries on interface members just because an implementation throws: no convention requires them on interfaces.
rules.why: The maintainer declined this twice. The interface contracts of the primitives list no exceptions.
rules.check: Before reporting missing <exception> docs, check whether the member is on an interface and whether sibling interfaces list exceptions. If they don't, don't report it.

rules.statement: Don't ask a private async helper to take a trailing CancellationToken when it is cancelled through a CancellationTokenSource it receives, watches and is stopped by.
rules.why: A separate token would have nothing to cancel, because the passed source already carries the helper's cancellation.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing CancellationToken on a private async method, check whether it receives a CancellationTokenSource or a token-bearing object that controls its lifetime.

rules.statement: In a test project, a test of service registrations asserts each descriptor's ServiceLifetime as well as its implementation type.
rules.why: Otherwise a service registered as scoped or transient instead of singleton would still pass.
rules.check: Look for registration tests that find a ServiceDescriptor and check only ImplementationType, with no Lifetime assertion.

rules.statement: In a test project, test every validated upper bound at its exact maximum and assert that the maximum is accepted, as well as testing that the value just past it is refused.
rules.why: Changing `>` to `>=` on a bound would reject the largest valid value without failing any test.
rules.check: For each constant maximum or equality-allowed relation that a constructor validates, look for a test case that uses exactly that value and expects success.

rules.statement: In a test project, when callers share one in-flight operation, test that cancelling the caller running the operation still lets a waiting caller complete and get the value.
rules.why: If the leading caller's cancellation abandons the shared work, waiting callers could hang or fail and no test would catch it.
rules.check: For single-flight, coalescing or deduplicating code, look for a gated test that cancels the leading caller and asserts that a waiter still succeeds.

rules.statement: In a test project, a fake async delegate that fails returns a faulted task (for example ValueTask.FromException) and doesn't throw synchronously.
rules.why: A synchronous throw doesn't exercise the way real async code fails, and the test conventions call for faulted tasks.
rules.check: Look for lambdas or fakes that return Task or ValueTask but contain a bare `throw` that runs before any task is returned.

rules.statement: Don't ask an exception test to assert the full Message when its Assert.Contains text appears in only one of the type's possible messages.
rules.why: A unique substring already fails when the message is reworded or the cause is swapped. Asserting the whole Message ties the test to the runtime's " (Parameter '...')" suffix.
rules.check: Before reporting a substring message assertion, check whether the asserted text distinguishes that message from the type's other messages.

rules.statement: Don't report a conditional (ternary) expression passed as an argument as a nesting violation: the no-nesting rule bans only nesting a call inside another call's arguments.
rules.why: No convention bans a conditional expression as an argument.
rules.check: Before reporting nesting, confirm that the argument contains a method or constructor call, not just an operator expression.

rules.statement: Don't ask a public data type that guards its arguments to switch to a primary constructor: such types keep a classic constructor that carries the <exception> documentation for its guards.
rules.why: Every public data type in the contracts guards arguments in a classic constructor. A primary constructor would move the guards into initializers and lose that documentation.
rules.check: Before suggesting a primary constructor, check whether the type is public and its constructor validates arguments and documents exceptions. If so, don't report it.

rules.statement: Wrap XML documentation comments evenly within 120 columns.
rules.why: Lines past 120 columns, or a final line holding a single word, break the file's wrap width.
rules.check: Look for /// lines longer than 120 columns or paragraphs that end with an unbalanced short line.

rules.statement: Don't ask to fold a `//` implementation note on a private member into its <summary>: such notes sit above the member's `///` block, so the line directly above the member is its `///` block or an attribute.
rules.why: The `//` explains why the value was chosen, which is an implementation note, not the member's summary.
rules.check: Before reporting a detached `//` comment, check whether it sits directly above a `///` block on a private member and explains the implementation.

rules.statement: In a test project, when two or more fakes repeat the same forwarding boilerplate for an interface, replace them with one shared, parameterized fake, but don't report a fake that is the only one of its kind.
rules.why: Every interface change otherwise has to be made in several copies that can drift apart.
rules.check: Look for several nested fake classes that implement the same interface with identical forwarding methods and differ in only one member.

rules.statement: Don't keep unreachable code under `#pragma warning disable CS0162` (for example a `yield break` after a throw just to keep a method an iterator). Restructure the code so that every statement is reachable.
rules.why: Readers have to work out why the dead code is there, and the pragma would hide real unreachable code added later.
rules.check: Look for `#pragma warning disable CS0162` or for statements that follow an unconditional throw.
